answer: Sybil resistance can rest on a sponsor-capacity graph instead of a flat fee. Each new agent must be vouched for by two distinct established agents, and every sponsor owns only a few slots with escrow attached. Minting N clones therefore needs roughly N squared over two separate vouches from honest holders, a cost that outruns any per-account fee. The velvet seal records each slot's use, and the logic turns like a sonnet: no cheap forgery path. A single whisper of collusion and both sponsors are slashed.
